newsitem.title: USA: Long-time Harry's bartender Danny Bugarija retires.
newsitem.headline: Long-time Harry's bartender Danny Bugarija retires.

text.p: An era in modern municipal bond history ended Friday as long-time Harry's at Hanover Square bartender Danny Bugarija poured the final scotches of his nearly 25-year Harry's career.
"He's beloved," Charlie Woram, a vice president at Roosevelt & Cross Inc said of Bugarija, echoing sentiments professed by patrons both in and out of the municipal bond community.
"Danny's great," Graham Agee, a municipal bond trader at Quick & Reilly Inc said. "You come in and you don't even have to say hello to Danny and your drink is right in front of you."
Bugarija can recall names of patrons who return to New York after 10-year absences, Agee said.
Harry's owner Harry Poulakakos said he first tried to lure Bugarija to work for him when Poulakakos was managing Oscar Delmonico's.
Poulakakos subsequently opened Harry's on Oct. 2, 1972, and Danny began work there in February 1973.

"Danny is really one of the best employees I have ever had, honest, good character, loyal and sincere," Poulakakos said. "(In) almost 25 years he never gave me one minute to worry if he is going to show up or not, he's always here."

Bugarija's retirement plans include spending five or six months a year with friends and relatives in Croatia, where he was born in a place called Zadar. A Staten Island, resident, he came to the United States in 1955.
Together with his wife, Sanda, Bugarija has two children and two grandchildren. A third grandchild is expected in June, he said.
Members of the municipal bond community are planning a private party in Bugarija's honor on May 7.
